scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7115: Hi, weird one: my computer refuses to talk to my
desk-mate's computer, even though we sit RIGHT NEXT to each other. Nothing
goes through AT ALL, in either direction. Something around the office switch
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at whatever connects
our two computers and make them friends again? We need to share files for
Friday!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC15 and PC16 are both on the Location B
  172.18.51.0/24 subnet, in the same broadcast domain -- a pure intra-subnet,
  Layer-2 path that does not involve router6 routing. PC15 reaches PC16 with 0%
  loss; the Location B switch forwards frames normally and PC16's port is up. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. (Note: this is intra-Location-B traffic,
  which is NOT subject to the router6 ACL 110 -- that policy only restricts
  Location A -> Location B, not B-internal traffic.) This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an L2/switch fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC15 cannot reach its
same-subnet Location B neighbor PC16 -- is NOT reproducible: both hosts sit on
172.18.51.0/24 in the same broadcast domain, and PC15 reaches PC16 directly (same
subnet, no routing) with 0% loss. The Location B switch forwards frames normally
and PC16's port is up. The router6 ACL 110 is irrelevant here -- it only limits
Location A -> Location B, not traffic internal to Location B.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-subnet L2 path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC15->PC16
path, finds it working, confirms both interfaces are up on the same subnet, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a switch drop, a downed port, or
(mistakenly) invokes the router6 ACL for B-internal traffic is over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC15 and PC16 are same-subnet (172.18.51.0/24) within Location B and reach each other with 0% loss at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected subsystem is the Layer-2 VLAN bridge configuration on **switch1**. The device running `bridge` has split its access ports into two completely separate bridge instances: **br_vlan10** (carrying ports eth1–eth6, where pc4, pc5, laptop2, and laptop3 are connected) and **br_vlan20** (carrying only eth7, where laptop0 is connected). laptop0 is literally the only end device in VLAN20 and in the 172.16.20.10/24 subnet; every other device on the same physical switch lives in VLAN10 (172.16.10.x/24).

Because laptop0 is in a completely separate bridge domain from its physical neighbours, all L2 mechanisms fail between them: ARP broadcasts from laptop0 never reach laptop2/laptop3/pc4/pc5 and vice versa, NetBIOS and mDNS-based file-sharing discovery don't cross the VLAN boundary, and SMB/CIFS cannot resolve or connect without broadcast-level reachability. This is why the desk-mates observe total silence — the office switch (switch1) is partitioning them even though they share the same physical chassis.

An inter-VLAN route via router0 (172.16.10.1 on eth0.10, 172.16.20.1 on eth0.20) exists and allows raw ICMP to pass with TTL=63, but that does not restore broadcast-domain membership needed for file sharing.

**Root cause:** switch1's port eth7 (laptop0's access port) is assigned to `br_vlan20` instead of `br_vlan10`, L2-isolating laptop0 from all other devices on the same physical switch.

**Fix:** On switch1, move eth7 from br_vlan20 to br_vlan10 (`brctl delif br_vlan20 eth7; brctl addif br_vlan10 eth7`), then reconfigure laptop0's IP from 172.16.20.10/24 (gw 172.16.20.1) to a free address in 172.16.10.0/24 (e.g., 172.16.10.10, gw 172.16.10.1). This places laptop0 in the same broadcast domain and subnet as its desk-mates.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC15 and PC16 are same-subnet (172.18.51.0/24) within Location B and reach each other with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The submission makes no mention of PC15/PC16 or that they are colocated on 172.18.51.0/24 and communicating with 0% loss, so it fails to acknowledge the baseline healthy condition.

The agent's logs show host IPs, successful ping results (with differing TTLs), bridge outputs that place laptop0 on a different bridge, and firewall/ebtables checks; the writeup's conclusion that laptop0 is L2-isolated by switch1's VLAN configuration follows logically from those observations and covers likely alternatives. Minor gaps: some outputs are truncated and the agent didn't explicitly show the exact eth7↔laptop0 port mapping in a single uncut snippet, but the overall evidence chain is strong.
